hebdo.accroche: Global security dynamics escalated sharply this week as Middle Eastern confrontations intensified with the downing of two US fighter jets and ballistic missile strikes on Saudi Arabia, whilst the tech sector was rocked by the resignation of Nvidia's CEO amid Chinese espionage revelations. Concurrently, European and Asian armed forces accelerated integrated air defence and counter-drone procurements alongside carrier-borne unmanned combat trials ahead of major trilateral summitry in Shenzhen.

tendances.titre: Accelerated fielding of multi-layered IAMD and C-UAS architectures
tendances.resume: European nations are moving swiftly to close air and drone defence gaps following NATO's failure to intercept an intruding drone over the Baltic states. Belgium crystallised its multilayered 'Blue Dome' architecture through firm contracts for Thales GM200 MM/C radars, Rheinmetall Skyranger 30 systems, and NASAMS batteries. In parallel, Poland selected Weibel XENTA-M5 radars for counter-UAV defence, whilst novel tactical solutions such as Beretta's LIVET automated turret and US palletised S-SHORAD sleds reflect an urgent pivot towards layered, mobile point defence.

tendances.titre: Direct kinetic escalation and critical infrastructure targeting across the Middle East
tendances.resume: Regional hostilities broadened beyond proxy exchanges, culminating in Iranian fire downing two US military aircraft and tanker mine explosions closing the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi air defences repeatedly engaged Houthi ballistic missile and drone salvos over Riyadh and Mecca following strikes on Aramco and critical pipeline infrastructure. Heightened Iranian threats also triggered the defensive dispersal of US air assets from British bases to Germany and forced the US military to engage Iranian drones over Bahrain.

Beijing has countered by warning Washington against further semiconductor controls, brandishing potential critical rare earth export caps.

tendances.titre: Manned-unmanned teaming and uncrewed strike platforms mature towards operational use
tendances.resume: Major powers achieved vital milestones in integrating autonomous combat systems into frontline strike doctrine. The US Air Force demonstrated live F-22 command of a YFQ-44A Collaborative Combat Aircraft, whilst the Royal Navy executed attack drone trials and scheduled Talon Blue CCA carrier flights aboard HMS Queen Elizabeth. Concurrently, China publicly showcased its GJ-11 stealth flying-wing combat drone, underscoring that airborne uncrewed teaming is now central to high-end air combat planning.

tendances.titre: Naval surface-to-air modularity and long-range asymmetric maritime strike
tendances.resume: Naval air defence and anti-surface warfare requirements are converging towards higher cross-platform modularity and longer stand-off ranges. The UK initiated feasibility studies to integrate MBDA Aster 30 interceptors into Lockheed Martin MK 41 vertical launch cells, whilst Saab unveiled the GaN-based Sea Giraffe AMB D radar. Demonstrating asymmetric naval vulnerability, Ukrainian long-range strike drones breached deep Baltic defences to hit and damage a Russian Buyan-M corvette in the Gulf of Finland.

Concurrently, Abu Dhabi hosted Ukraine peace negotiations where Moscow agreed to formal European participation following prisoner exchanges, despite ongoing Russian infrastructure bombardment. In the Indo-Pacific, Beijing paired diplomatic engagement with sustained coercive pressure, running unannounced carrier strike group area-denial exercises east of Taiwan.
